nodes.title: Keep the last deps and value in a ref

anchor.snippet: const cache = useRef<{ deps: readonly unknown[]; value: T } | null>(null);

nodes.why: A ref survives renders without causing them, which is exactly what a memo cache needs.
nodes.alternative: Keep the cached value in useState.
nodes.tradeoff: State would trigger an extra render whenever the cache refreshes; a ref does not.

nodes.title: Compare dependencies with Object.is
nodes.why: React compares memo dependencies with Object.is, so NaN equals NaN and +0 and -0 differ.
nodes.tradeoff: === treats NaN as changed forever, and JSON.stringify is slow and loses functions.

nodes.title: Recompute when the number of dependencies changes
nodes.why: A different dependency count means a different call site shape, so the cache cannot be trusted.
nodes.tradeoff: Ignoring extra entries would hide real changes.

nodes.title: Call the factory only on the first render or a change
nodes.why: The factory runs during render, like React's own useMemo, and its result is reused until a dependency changes.
nodes.alternative: Run the factory in an effect and store the result.
nodes.tradeoff: An effect would render the stale value first and then render again.

nodes.title: Load once in the provider, not in every consumer
nodes.why: Three consumers read the same context value, so there is one request per load instead of one per component.
nodes.tradeoff: Fetching in the hook multiplies requests by the number of consumers.

nodes.title: Ignore a response from an older load
nodes.why: A slow response from a previous load must not overwrite the result of a newer one.
nodes.alternative: Trust that responses arrive in order.
nodes.tradeoff: Order is not guaranteed on real networks; the flag costs one line.

nodes.title: Turn a rejection into an error state
nodes.why: Consumers can render a readable error instead of waiting forever.
nodes.tradeoff: An unhandled rejection leaves every consumer stuck on loading.

nodes.title: Reload by bumping a counter the effect depends on
nodes.why: The effect already knows how to load; a counter re-runs it without duplicating the request code, and useCallback keeps reload stable.
nodes.tradeoff: A direct call needs its own loading, error and stale handling.

nodes.title: Memoize the context value with your own hook

anchor.snippet: const value = useMemoized(() => ({ state, reload }), [state, reload]);

nodes.why: A new object on every provider render would re-render every consumer; memoizing keeps the value stable until state changes.
nodes.tradeoff: Inline objects are simpler but defeat React.memo on consumers.

nodes.title: Fail loudly outside the provider
nodes.why: A clear error beats a silent default that looks like an endless loading state.
nodes.tradeoff: Defaults hide wiring mistakes; an error names them.
